## Introduction

My data visualization project leverages the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) dataset to answer the question: when did computer science (CS) become such a popular undergraduate degree, and how has its popularity varied geographically and across institutions?

This question is motivated and informed by the previous data projects I have worked on as part of my job in higher education administration. Of course, the "learn-to-code" phenomenon is a ubiquitous topic in higher education. Yet, I was still surprised to see the dramatic national trend in CS degrees in the dataset.

Furthermore, as part of my previous IPEDS data project, I struggled to visualize the rich degrees granted IPEDS dataset efficiently. I wanted to maximize users' freedom to discover trends in the data across institutions. However, many visualizations used line plots, with multiple institutions shown in different colors, producing a "rainbow spaghetti" effect that obscured trends and likely discouraged exploration. Thus, for this project, I wanted to begin with a more focused question and a better understanding of effective visualization design, informed by Dr. Albers Szafir’s lectures.
